title: Polymorphic genera vary in traits of no use, unfixed by selection

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Polymorphic genera vary in traits of no use, unfixed by selection

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In polymorphic genera such as Rubus, Rosa and Hieracium, the inordinate variation concerns structures that are of no service or disservice to the species and so have not been seized on and made definite by natural selection.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: I am inclined to suspect that we see in these polymorphic genera variations in points of structure which are of no service or disservice to the species, and which consequently have not been seized on and rendered definite by natural selection

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter II, “Variation under Nature”; section “Individual Differences”. Scope: polymorphic genera of plants, insects and brachiopods

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch02-02: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.54

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Neutrality is operationalizable but requires direct fitness data, not merely high variation. Public observations and study datasets permit limited tests, while the general causal attribution remains confounded.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Within polymorphic genera, estimate fitness effects and selection gradients for highly variable structures, comparing them with less variable traits. Near-zero effects coupled with persistent variation support the claim; consistent positive or negative selection refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Fitness effects are environment dependent.

Trait-fitness data for the named genera are sparse.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.42
operationalizability: 0.63

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Floras and trait databases can show which groups and characters are polymorphic. They do not contain an independent measure of service or disservice, so the selective explanation is weakly identified. A non-circular test would need fitness data that are still study-specific and taxonomically narrow.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Within polymorphic genera such as Rubus, Rosa, and Hieracium, compare selection gradients or functional effects of characters that vary excessively with characters that are stable. The suspicion would be supported if the variable characters had gradients indistinguishable from zero while stable characters did not; strong selection on the variable characters would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Inferring that a character is useless because it is unfixed makes the test circular.

Selection gradients for Rubus, Rosa, and Hieracium are not compiled in an open trait database.

Apomixis and taxonomic oversplitting create polymorphism that has nothing to do with the selective value of a structure.
